Exploratory Data Analysis
Conflict Data from ACLED

Varvara Ilyina

May 24, 2024

Requirements

What are some of the most important patterns in your data that you can observe through exploratory data analysis? For instance, what does the label look like? What do the simple bivariate relationships in the data look like? Will this affect any of your modeling choices?


Setup

## load packages
pacman::p_load(reticulate, tidyverse, haven, readxl, writexl, stringr, ggplot2, sf, maps, viridis, modelsummary, gt, knitr, kableExtra, janitor, corrplot, report)

## set working directory
#project_root_dir <- py$project_root_dir
#setwd(project_root_dir)

#setwd("/Users/varvarailyina/hertie/ML/US_conflict_forecasting/")
getwd()


## set colors
#COL2 <- colorRampPalette(c("goldenrod3", "white", "purple1"))


## create theme for ggplot
angle_theme <- theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
                     axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 1, size = 12),
                     axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
                     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
                     plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
                     plot.caption = element_text(),
                     legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
                     legend.key.size = unit(2, 'lines'),
                     legend.title = element_blank())


Import / clean data

## load final dataset
data_final_raw <- read.csv("../2_Dataset/d_Final_Dataset/Final_Dataset_Lag.csv", sep = ",")

## clean data
data <- data_final_raw %>% janitor::clean_names()


## load all ACLED data
data_acled_all <- read.csv("../2_Dataset/a_Input_Datasets/US2020_2023.csv", sep = ",")


Choose important features

## select features marked as important for EDA
codebook <- read_excel("./codebook_clean.xlsx") %>%
  filter(important == 1) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = var_name,
              values_from = var_length) %>%
  select(-c(1:6)) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

## vector with important vars
vars_keep <- names(codebook)


Zip codes with most events

## calculate number of events per zip code
df <- data %>%
  select(zcta, month, event_count) %>%
  filter(event_count > 0) %>%
  group_by(zcta) %>%
  summarize(tot_events = sum(event_count)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(zcta, tot_events) %>%
  unique() %>%
  arrange(desc(tot_events))

## df with zip code names and pop
df_tmp <- data %>%
  select(zcta, admin2, post_office_city_name, total_population_2022, population_per_square_land_mile_2022) %>%
  unique() %>%
  
  # remove ", PA" from city names
  mutate(post_office_city_name = str_extract(post_office_city_name, "^.*(?=(,))"))


## merge names onto zip code df
df_all <- left_join(df, df_tmp, by = "zcta") %>%
  filter(tot_events > 4)


caption <- "Only post office city names in Pennsylvania with more than 5 conflicts in 2022 included, \n where post office city names correspond with unique zip codes"

## plot event freq by zip
p <- ggplot(df_all, aes(reorder(post_office_city_name, -tot_events), tot_events, fill = factor(post_office_city_name))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", fill = "steelblue3") +
  labs(title = "Number of Conflicts per PA Zip Code in 2022",
       #subtitle = "Ordered in decreasing order",
       x = "",
       y = "Number of Conflicts",
       caption = caption) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(df_all$tot_events + 20))) +
  #geom_text(aes(post_office_city_name, tot_events, label = str_c(tot_events, " %")),
  geom_text(aes(post_office_city_name, tot_events, label = tot_events),
            position = position_dodge(0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  angle_theme + theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p)


## plot pop density for zips with most events
p <- ggplot(df_all, aes(reorder(admin2, -tot_events), population_per_square_land_mile_2022, fill = factor(admin2))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", fill = "steelblue3") +
  labs(title = "Number of Conflicts in 
       Population in PA Counties with Highest Number of Conflicts in 2022",
       #subtitle = "subtitle",
       x = "",
       y = "Population",
       caption = "Only includes counties with more than 5 conflicts in 2022") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(df_all$population_per_square_land_mile_2022 + 20))) +
  #geom_text(aes(admin2, tot_events, label = str_c(tot_events, " %")),
  geom_text(aes(admin2, tot_events, label = tot_events),
            position = position_dodge(0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  angle_theme + theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p)


Months with most events

## create df with total events per month
df <- data %>%
  select(zcta, month, event_count) %>%
  filter(event_count > 0) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(tot_events = sum(event_count)) %>%
  ungroup()


## plot event freq by month
p <- ggplot(df, aes(month, tot_events, fill = factor(month))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", fill = "steelblue3") +
  labs(title = "Number of Conflicts per Month in PA in 2022",
       x = "",
       y = "Number of Conflicts") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(df$tot_events + 20))) +
  geom_text(aes(month, tot_events, label = tot_events),
            position = position_dodge(0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  angle_theme + theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p)


Events across US states - table

df <- data_acled_all %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  select(event_id_cnty, event_date, admin1)

df %>%
  group_by(admin1) %>%
  rename(us_state = admin1) %>%
  mutate(tot_events_2022 = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(us_state, tot_events_2022) %>%
  unique() %>%
  arrange(desc(tot_events_2022)) %>%
  slice(1:10) %>%

Events across US states - map

df <- data_acled_all %>%
  filter(year == 2022) %>%
  select(event_id_cnty, event_date, admin1)

df_tmp <- df %>%
  group_by(admin1) %>%
  rename(us_state = admin1) %>%
  mutate(tot_events_2022 = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(us_state, tot_events_2022) %>%
  unique() %>%
  arrange(desc(tot_events_2022))

## get us states map data
us_states <- map_data("state")

## convert state names to lowercase to match the map data
df_tmp$us_state <- tolower(df_tmp$us_state)

## merge the event data with the map data
map_data <- us_states %>%
  left_join(df_tmp, by = c("region" = "us_state"))

# Create the heat map
p <- ggplot(data = map_data, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = tot_events_2022)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1, na.value = "white") +
  labs(title = "Number of Conflict Events by US State in 2022",
       fill = "Event Count",
       x = "",
       y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# Print the plot
print(p)
